correctness.rationale: The ratios are affine invariants; near the centroid the body has positive volume exactly for t>1/4. Independently, inclusion-exclusion in the barycentric affine hyperplane gives the normalized volume of the slice a≤lambda_i≤b as F(a,b)=sum_j (-1)^j binom(4,j)[1-4a-j(b-a)]_+^3. Its derivatives are the sums of the supporting facet area times altitude, with the lower sign negative. Center at barycentric (1/4,...,1/4); reflection moves the lower and upper support planes of K_t at rates 1/4-max(lambda_i) and 1/4-min(lambda_i), respectively. Differentiating F in that direction at (0,t) therefore gives 3M_t/V_T by first variation; inactive planes contribute zero. In the first simplex chamber min(lambda_i)=1-3t, max=t; in the two middle chambers min=0, max=t; in the final simplex chamber min=0, max=1. The resulting V and M polynomials match the frozen formulas in all open chambers, and extend to the common endpoints by continuity. In particular t=1/2 is the centrally symmetric affine octahedron. For rho=M/V, the sign of the two derivative factors is settled by expanding at 1/3 and at 1 (the latter has positive lower bound 1+6s-8s^2 for s in [0,1/2]). This gives strict decrease then increase with unique minimum 1, ratio 3 on the two simplex branches. Minkowski expansion gives difference-body ratio 2+6rho. The exact left/right series around t=1/2 have common quadratic coefficient 32 and cubic coefficients -32 and -224; distinct slopes of rho'' give no third derivative there and jump -1152. For t<1/4 there is no feasible point, at equality only the centroid, so the normalized ratio is undefined there. The prior Godbersen results give universal inequalities and equality cases, not this polynomial specialization; they are not the basis for the overlap.

evidence: In barycentric coordinates the descending vertex representative greedily fills each coordinate up to t until the total is one. Its partial sums are min(jt,1), which majorize every feasible vector; equivalently every vertex is a permutation of this representative since all but at most one coordinate are at bounds. Its orbit hull is exactly Postnikov's permutohedron, including repeated entries. Normalizing by the original simplex removes the constant affine volume factor.

Reversal of the three adjacent coordinate gaps is reflection up to translation. The Minkowski sum with a multiple of the reflection adds the two hypersimplex-weight vectors, so the two volumes are encoded in one polynomial.

value.rationale: This is a natural deformation between simplices and an octahedron, and the elementary facet proof is correct. But the proposed scientific invariant is an exact prior P4 polynomial specialization. Reexpressing it, checking the sign of the derivative, and reporting a cubic coefficient jump for this one rational function do not yield a distinct mathematical remainder warranting repair.
